title: Research Engine Local Document Intelligence and Compute Offload v1
goal: Design, benchmark, and integrate a provenance-preserving local document-intelligence pipeline that converts content-addressed research PDFs into reusable LLM-ready paper packages, minimizes paid/plan semantic usage and repeated PDF interpretation, and systematically evaluates every research-engine stage for safe deterministic or local-model offload before production deployment on the Lambda.
acceptance_criteria: A versioned paper-package.v1 contract exists and preserves the original PDF SHA-256 as scientific authority while representing normalized reading-order Markdown, page/block provenance, extracted figures, tables, equations, references/citations, diagnostics, confidence, and parser/model lineage.

The pipeline uses a cascaded cost model: deterministic/native PDF extraction first, specialized local OCR/layout/table/formula/document models only where needed, and a general local VLM/agent only for low-confidence or structurally difficult regions.

Every document transformation is content-addressed and cacheable so a PDF is compiled once per parser/model/config version and reused by future EXTRACT, VERIFY, synthesis, retrieval, and research runs.

Mathpix Markdown is usable as a non-production reference oracle generated manually by the user under the user's approximately 60,000-page/year desktop allowance; no Mathpix paid API dependency is introduced into production.

A reproducible benchmark corpus covers born-digital multi-column papers, scanned pages, equations, easy and complex tables, figures/charts, mixed layouts, references, malformed text layers, and representative research-engine papers.

Candidate local stacks are compared with objective document metrics and downstream research metrics, including reading order, text fidelity, equation fidelity, table structure/cell fidelity, figure-caption association, provenance/page mapping, output token count, pages/second, CPU/RAM/GPU/VRAM, cold-start/model-load cost, and failure rate.

The benchmark evaluates current local candidates/components including at least native PDF extraction plus Docling, MinerU, PaddleOCR/PP-StructureV3, and Marker/Surya or documented successors, without assuming one monolithic converter must win every stage.
A page/region triage policy classifies native-text, OCR-required, table/formula/chart, and ambiguous regions and records why each region was routed to a given local processor.

Concurrent ingestion is validated with a shared local inference service or equivalent scheduler that avoids loading duplicate large models per PDF worker and supports bounded batching/backpressure under multiple simultaneous documents.

Figure handling separates extraction from semantic interpretation: figures/images and captions are always preserved with provenance, while expensive chart/figure understanding runs only when needed by downstream evidence extraction or low-confidence parsing.
Research-engine EXTRACT and VERIFY can consume paper-package.v1-derived context while retaining a fail-closed path back to authoritative PDF pages/regions for verification.

A/B evaluation on the preserved research corpus demonstrates downstream evidence/provenance agreement versus the current PDF path and measures total semantic-token/plan-allowance savings; a parser is not accepted solely for pretty Markdown.

The task includes an explicit localization matrix for every research-engine stage/substage, deciding deterministic-local, specialized-local-model, general-local-model, external/web-dependent, or remote-strong-reasoning based on measured quality and throughput rather than convenience.

Any localization of semantic jobs such as SCREEN, EXTRACT, VERIFY, retrieval/ranking, or embeddings is benchmark-gated; high-level novelty arbitration, gap generation, synthesis, and web-dependent discovery/search remain remote/external unless evidence demonstrates a safe local replacement.

Selected implementation passes canonical GitHub CI and a separate Lambda acceptance test with the actual production hardware/software environment, including concurrency, dependency/model installation, model caching, restart behavior, and resource ceilings.
Production document compilation requires no per-page paid OCR API and no OPENAI_API_KEY; external services may remain optional benchmark/reference tools only.
Licensing, model/data-use restrictions, weight redistribution constraints, and operational dependencies are documented before a candidate is promoted into the production research engine.
Benchmark and production artifacts preserve enough diagnostics to reproduce routing and failures without treating generated Markdown/JSON as scientific authority.
constraints: Keep research-engine-daemon.service inactive/dead during this task's benchmark and integration work unless a later capsule checkpoint explicitly opens a bounded runtime validation gate.
Do not START sustained corpus expansion merely to benchmark document parsing.
Do not introduce Mathpix API billing or make Mathpix an unattended production dependency; the user's desktop Mathpix conversion can be used manually as a high-quality benchmark oracle.
Do not treat Mathpix output as ground truth where the original PDF disagrees; the PDF remains authoritative.
Do not send every born-digital page through OCR/VLM by default. Native text/layout extraction must be attempted and quality-scored first.
Do not run a general vision/reasoning agent on every page as the default architecture; broad VLM use must be an escalation path justified by confidence or document structure.
Do not destroy page/block/figure/table/equation provenance when normalizing to Markdown or JSON.
Do not duplicate heavyweight model instances per concurrent document when a shared/batched inference service can provide higher throughput and lower VRAM pressure.
Do not optimize only single-document latency. Benchmark sustained multi-document throughput and queue/backpressure behavior.
Do not commit large source PDFs, model weights, or high-volume production artifacts to workspace-control. Use the research-engine artifact store or user-provided files for bulky data.

GitHub may be used during development for code, benchmark manifests, textual outputs, metrics, and representative small fixtures; it must not become the high-frequency production document-artifact store.
Do not silently replace the current EXTRACT/VERIFY path until downstream evidence and provenance equivalence are measured on representative preserved papers.
Do not conflate token savings with plan-allowance savings; retain exact token telemetry and censored allowance observations as separate measurements.
Prefer direct GitHub tooling for repository work; use the Lambda terminal only for genuine runtime/hardware/model validation boundaries.
Every fresh-chat initialization/handoff for this task must include https://github.com/adamtrott78/workspace-control.

New operator-facing temporary, benchmark, diagnostic, and handoff artifacts that may need human download must be written under the visible ~/adamArchives/Adam/workspace-control-tmp/ root (or explicit WORKSPACE_CONTROL_TMP_ROOT). Existing ~/.workspace-control/tmp artifacts are legacy inputs only and must not be moved or regenerated solely for visibility.
